How this blog works

Everything a post can contain — headings, equations, code, figures and interactive plots. Delete this file once you have your own posts.

A post is one markdown file in src/research-blog/posts/. The front matter at the top sets the title, subtitle and date; everything below it is ordinary markdown. Drop the file in, save, and it appears on the index — no list to update, no HTML to write.

Front matter #

Only title and date are required.

---
title: Star formation in ultra-faint dwarfs
subtitle: One line that shows up under the title and on the index card.
date: 2026-09-18
tags: ["simulations", "enzo"]
image: images/posts/sfrd-hero.png   # optional; otherwise the first image is used
draft: true                          # hidden from production builds
---

Setting draft: true keeps a post visible while you run npm start but leaves it out of the built site, so you can write in the open branch without publishing.

Equations #

Inline math sits between single dollar signs — the escape fraction fescf_{\rm esc}fesc​ is the usual suspect — and display math between double ones:

ρ˙⋆(z)  =  ∫Mmin∞dndM M˙⋆(M,z) dM\dot{\rho}_\star(z) \;=\; \int_{M_{\rm min}}^{\infty} \frac{\mathrm{d}n}{\mathrm{d}M}\, \dot{M}_\star(M, z)\, \mathrm{d}M ρ˙​⋆​(z)=∫Mmin​∞​dMdn​M˙⋆​(M,z)dM

These are rendered with KaTeX at build time, so the published page is plain HTML — nothing to download, and it still reads correctly if a visitor blocks scripts.

Code #

Fenced blocks are highlighted during the build:

import numpy as np
import yt

ds = yt.load("DD0100/DD0100")
ad = ds.all_data()

# star formation rate density in a 1 Mpc/h box
masses = ad["all", "particle_mass"].in_units("Msun")
ages = ad["all", "age"].in_units("Myr")
sfrd = masses[ages < 10].sum() / (10e6 * ds.domain_width.in_units("Mpc")[0] ** 3)
print(f"SFRD = {sfrd:.3e}")

Short spans of inline code work the usual way.

Figures #

Use the img shortcode so images get a caption, lazy loading and a click-to-zoom viewer, and so a missing file falls back to a placeholder instead of breaking the build:

{% img "images/posts/halo-profile.png",
       "Density profile of a simulated halo",
       "NFW fit to a z = 6 halo, 1024³ run" %}

Interactive plots #

Export a Plotly figure from Python straight into the repo:

import plotly.io as pio
pio.write_json(fig, "src/files/plots/sfrd.json")

then drop it into a post:

{% plotly "files/plots/sfrd.json" %}

plotly.js is only fetched on pages that actually contain a figure, and the plot restyles itself when the page switches between light and dark.

Everything else #

Standard markdown all works: bold, italic, links, blockquotes, tables and footnotes[1].

Run Resolution Box size
A 512³ 10 Mpc/h
B 1024³ 10 Mpc/h

Blockquotes are useful for pulling a result out of the surrounding text.

  1. Footnotes land at the bottom of the post with a link back up. ↩︎
